paper.title: Large independent sets on random d-regular graphs with fixed degree d
paper.relevant_claim_for_degree_3: The paper reports an asymptotic independence ratio of about 0.445330(3) for its deferred-decision algorithm on random 3-regular graphs; this is an algorithmic lower-bound result on its workload, not a finite-instance upper bound or proof of MIS optimality.

license_audit.decision: Do not vendor, copy, or redistribute source code until reuse permission/license is clarified. Public availability alone does not grant an open-source license.
license_audit.safe_next_step: Treat the pinned repository as an external executable reference only if its owner-approved reuse terms allow it; otherwise implement a clean-room Rust reimplementation from the published paper and validate it independently.

role_in_qcomp.why_it_matters: The 2026 quantum-enhanced greedy MIS paper explicitly compares to the Marino-Kirkpatrick linear-time prioritized/deferred-decision algorithm. A minimal-degree greedy win is therefore not sufficient evidence of beating the strongest classical baseline for this track.
role_in_qcomp.fixed_graph_compatibility: The paper's algorithm co-generates a random regular graph and the independent-set labeling through deferred decisions and virtual-node operations. Do not presume it is a fixed-input graph solver. Establish its native input/output contract before choosing the statistical comparison.
recommended_comparison_design: Track A: for completed graph bytes shared by every policy, compare methods that accept fixed graphs and use paired graph-instance inference.

Track B: run a faithful deferred-decision implementation on its native generated-graph distribution; preserve and independently verify each generated graph and solution, then compare distribution-level outcomes with correctly specified unpaired inference.
Do not match seed integers to claim pairs unless the completed graph bytes are identical.
Report independence ratio, absolute set cardinality, graph size/degree, source generation, runtime and memory, random seed, algorithm revision and raw result digest.

qaoa_2026_context.title: A scalable quantum-enhanced greedy algorithm for maximum independent set problems on random regular graphs
qaoa_2026_context.relevance: The paper reports statistically significant p=4 improvements against the prioritized baseline for the considered sizes up to N <= 2000, while its paper text also notes the finite-size simulations had not yet exceeded the asymptotic 0.445330 value. These are external published claims, not Symthaea results.

validation_boundary: This manifest pins public source metadata only. It does not establish the source license, run the C++ code, reproduce the paper, validate a fixed-graph adapter, or demonstrate a SOTA result or quantum advantage.
